page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and text processing rates reaching the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations represent a significant tradeoff. Stress-ng multi-core performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores in the bottom 10% and uncached memory read/write bandwidths categorized in the bottom 25%.

Given its resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the c4-highcpu-4 is structured for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, and moderate web serving, where it achieves an average static web serving throughput of 8.75 GB/sec. It can handle basic LLM inference for small models, though text generation on medium models drops to the bottom 10%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a specialized, lower-cost entry point for compute-bound tasks that can leverage its advanced Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets without paying for excess memory.
